SpatialConvergence.ClaimBoundary: This is the manufactured nonmatching trace-projection rate. Full three-dimensional rod-shell solution convergence is reported separately.

TimeAndEventConvergence.ClaimBoundary: The rate audit uses a smooth oscillator and a unilateral zero-crossing canonical. Full wing deployment rates are a separate application matrix.

NativeLargeAssembly.ClaimBoundary: This is a native-connectivity linearized Cosserat rod-shell-mortar sparse assembly and a sparse-direct reference KKT solve. It is not a repeated small matrix and does not qualify the full nonlinear 100k-DOF Newton path.

NativeNonlinearScaling.ClaimBoundary: This qualifies repeated nonlinear residual/tangent assembly and sparse KKT Newton solves on native shell-triangle, rod-edge and Mortar connectivity. The nonlinear edge energy is an analytic scaling canonical; it does not replace the full production Cosserat rod and shell constitutive tangent or independently validate the wing.

Source.OriginalMethod: Simo and Vu-Quoc geometrically exact beam
Source.Geometry: radius 100 m, arc 45 deg, unit square section

PublicBenchmark.ClaimBoundary: This qualifies the rod constitutive/kinematic route against a public large-rotation benchmark. It does not independently validate the shell, Mortar interface, UVLM, or complete deployable wing.

IndependentMortarReference.ClaimBoundary: This is an independent six-field flat-interface manufactured reference for nonmatching P1/P1 traces and a P0 multiplier. It checks displacement, rotation, force, moment and adjoint power transfer without sharing the production assembly. It is not an external curved-shell, full-wing or physical validation.

IndependentCurvedMortarReference.ClaimBoundary: This independently checks a curved, eccentric, finite-width Mortar constraint, its tangent, reactions and power transfer. It does not constitute a third-party full-wing structural or experimental validation.

ProductionSparseCosserat.ClaimBoundary: This qualifies the complete production reference rod and shell energies with element-local exact AD tangents above 10^4 KKT unknowns. It does not yet claim a 10^5-DoF full-production Newton solve or hand-coded analytic shell tangent.

FullWingMeshTimeConvergence.ClaimBoundary: All three mesh levels use the nonlinear production full-nodal Cosserat rod/shell/interface/hinge equilibrium. The time-step study uses the consistent constrained Lagrangian linearization about the finest nonlinear equilibrium with a smooth pulse; it does not replace the separate nonlinear event-resolved release and stop-impact qualification.

SectionParameterDerivation.Derivation: plane-stress shell resultants plus the stiffness increment of the central solid band represented as a rectangular rod section

ThirdPartyCurvedEquilibrium.ClaimBoundary: This is an independent linearized small-strain in-plane equilibrium of a curved composite strip, compared using a third-party 3D solid finite-element library. The production response is one tangent solve at its stress-free curved reference, with the reported nonlinear residual-to-load audit. It is not a third-party finite-rotation shell, impact, full-wing or experimental validation.

ThirdPartyDiscrepancyClosure.ClaimBoundary: The signed decomposition follows the declared sequence from the production finest response through longitudinal extrapolation, plane-stress-mapped and three-dimensional aligned solids, and the legacy solid discretization. It is an auditable model-form error budget, not a unique causal or experimentally calibrated split.

IndependentReferenceMeshConvergence.ClaimBoundary: The three independent Q2 levels stage arc-length refinement followed by finite-width refinement. One Q2 element is retained through thickness, so this is not an isotropic h-convergence rate or a through-thickness convergence claim.

NonlinearFullWingConvergence.ClaimBoundary: This matrix exercises nonlinear full-DOF rod-shell coupling, hinge release and event-localized lower-stop impact. It is a numerical convergence study, not experimental flight validation.

PublishedMethod.ComparedClass: BTS-FULL-CONS centerline-to-surface constant-normal-distance and rotational coupling with weighted penalty regularization

SharedCurvedEquilibrium.Benchmark: same curved production rod-shell tangent, root constraints and tip load with a zero-resultant transverse load gradient

SteinbrecherDirectComparison.ClaimBoundary: The comparison uses one curved structural tangent, load and boundary set to contrast the finite-width exact multiplier with an independently coded BTS-FULL-CONS centerline equation class and weighted penalties. It is not a rerun of the Steinbrecher software or a reproduction of its full examples.

OverRichMultiplierFailure.Reason: multiplier space is richer than both trace spaces
